subtitle: How the Horse-Doctor’s Science Rode Beside Kings

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Shalihotra Vaidya beside a powerful warhorse in a royal stable, distant outline of a marching army beyond the doorway
panels.action: Shalihotra Vaidya stands calm, hand on the neck of a tense warhorse in a dim royal stable, while beyond the open archway rows of mailed cavalry blur in dusty sunlight, readying to ride.

dialogue.text: As kings rode to war and merchants to distant seas, the Shalihotra tradition asked a quiet question: who will heal the horse that carries an empire’s weight?

i18n.hi: जब राजा युद्ध को निकले, सेठ समुंदर पार, शालिहोत्र परंपरा ने पूछा – साम्राज्य ढोते घोड़े को कौन चंगेगा?

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye of the Indian subcontinent, with trade routes and cavalry lines sketched as trails of dust and ships
panels.action: A sweeping view of the subcontinent shows caravan lines through deserts, ships along the coasts, and cavalry columns threading river valleys, all converging on busy royal cities.

dialogue.text: From the passes of the northwest to the ports of the eastern seas, horses stitched the subcontinent together—bearing kings, couriers, caravans and the hopes of states.

i18n.hi: उत्तर-पश्चिमी दर्रों से पूरब के बंदरगाहों तक, घोड़े ने भूभाग सी दिया – राजे, दूत, कारवां और राज्यों की आस ढोते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a royal stable, with scribes and grooms around Shalihotra Vaidya examining a horse’s leg
panels.action: In a large wooden stable, Shalihotra Vaidya kneels by a horse’s foreleg, fingers probing a swollen joint, while grooms hold the reins and a young scribe watches with a palm-leaf manuscript in hand.

dialogue.text: Here, away from the clash of spears, another battle unfolded—against lameness, fever and exhaustion—and men we now call Shalihotra-vaidyas turned care of horses into learned craft.

i18n.hi: भाले-तलवारों से दूर, दूसरी जंग थी – लंगड़ापन, बुखार, थकावट के खिलाफ – जहां शालिहोत्र-वैद्य कहे जाने वाले लोग घोड़े की सेवा को विद्या बनाते गए।

panels.shot: close-up of Ashoka’s rock edict being carved, with workers on scaffolding chiseling Brahmi letters into a boulder
panels.action: Artisans cling to scaffolding around a massive boulder as a master mason carefully chisels neat Brahmi letters, while an overseer points to the line speaking of healing for humans and animals.

dialogue.text: Centuries before the name Shalihotra appears in manuscripts, a Mauryan king had his will carved in stone: that medicines be provided for humans and for animals.

i18n.hi: शालिहोत्र नाम ग्रंथों में आने से भी सदियों पहले, एक मौर्य राजा ने पत्थर पर लिखवाया – इंसान ही नहीं, जानवरों को भी औषधि मिले।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Mauryan officer reading the freshly carved rock edict to villagers and stable-hands with a few horses tethered nearby
panels.action: A Mauryan official in simple robes stands before the carved rock, reading aloud to gathered villagers and stable-grooms as a pair of horses flick their ears in the shade.

dialogue.text: Ashoka’s Major Rock Edict II speaks of herbs, wells and care that should reach cattle and other beasts—a rare state promise, joining human and animal in a single policy of health.

i18n.hi: अशोक का प्रमुख शिला-लेख द्वितीय जड़ी-बूटियों, कुओं और देखभाल की बात करता है, जो गाय-भैंस और बाकी पशुओं तक पहुँचे – विरली शाही प्रतिज्ञा, जो मनुष्य और पशु की एक-साथ सेहत मांगती है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Shalihotra Vaidya seated cross-legged with palm-leaf manuscripts, a ghostly montage of later scribes around him to hint layered tradition
panels.action: Shalihotra Vaidya sits cross-legged, stylus poised over a palm leaf, while faint, overlapping images of later scribes in different dress copy and annotate similar leaves around him.

dialogue.text: The Shalihotra Samhita and other Ashvayurveda works grew over time; one revered name, many hands and ages, all weaving observations into a long, layered memory of the horse.

i18n.hi: शालिहोत्र संहिता और बाकी अश्वायुर्वेद ग्रंथ समय के साथ बढ़े – एक पूज्य नाम, पर अनेक हाथ और युग, जो घोड़ों पर देखी बातों को लम्बी, परतदार स्मृति में बुनते गए।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Shalihotra Vaidya writing, with illustrations of horse anatomy on the mat beside him
panels.action: Seen from behind, Shalihotra Vaidya inscribes neat lines on a palm leaf while beside him lie simple line drawings of a horse’s skeleton, muscles and internal organs.

dialogue.text: These texts begin with the body itself—bones, joints, veins, teeth—so that the healer knows what lies under skin before he names a single disease.

i18n.hi: ये ग्रंथ देह से शुरू होते हैं – हड्डियाँ, जोड़, नसें, दाँत – ताकि वैद्य त्वचा के नीचे को जाने, फिर किसी रोग का नाम ले।

panels.shot: medium shot in a stable as Shalihotra Vaidya demonstrates to apprentices how to inspect a horse’s mouth and eyes
panels.action: In a lamplit stable, Shalihotra Vaidya gently lifts a horse’s lip to show its teeth while two apprentices watch closely; another holds a small oil lamp up to the animal’s eye.

dialogue.text: He teaches apprentices to read signs: eyes clouded or clear, breath hot or cool, tongue dry, gums pale, gait uneven—a language of illness without words.

i18n.hi: वह शिष्यों को लक्षण पढ़ना सिखाता है – आँख धुंधली या साफ, साँस गरम या ठंडी, जीभ सूखी, मसूड़े फीके, चाल डगमग – बिना शब्दों की बीमारी की भाषा।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling royal stable yard, with different horses and grooms as Shalihotra Vaidya walks through inspecting
panels.action: In a wide courtyard lined with stalls, grooms curry sweating horses, fill mangers and sweep dung while Shalihotra Vaidya walks slowly down the line, hand brushing flanks, eye noting each animal’s condition.

dialogue.text: The Shalihotra corpus does not stop at herbs and charms; it speaks of fodder, grooming, stabling, exercise, of how space, feed and work must fit each animal’s nature.

i18n.hi: शालिहोत्र ग्रंथ जड़ी-बूटियों व टोनों पर ही नहीं रुकते; चारे, संवार, अस्तबल, कसरत की बात करते हैं – कैसे जगह, खाना और काम हर घोड़े के स्वभाव से मेल खाए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shalihotra Vaidya instructing on stable design, gesturing to ventilation slats, drainage and clean bedding
panels.action: Standing by a half-built stall, Shalihotra Vaidya points to wide ventilation slats, a sloped stone floor and neatly laid straw as carpenters and labourers adjust beams and troughs.

dialogue.text: He insists on air and dryness, on sweeping and sunlight; on how poor stables invite coughs, sores and pests that no medicine alone can drive away.

i18n.hi: वह हवा और सूखेपन पर जोर देता है, झाड़ू और धूप पर – कैसे गंदे अस्तबल खाँसी, घाव और कीड़े बुलाते हैं, जिन्हें अकेली दवा नहीं भगा सकती।

panels.shot: close-up of Shalihotra Vaidya preparing herbal medicines, grinding and mixing plant materials in bowls
panels.action: At a low stone bench, Shalihotra Vaidya grinds roots and leaves in a mortar, then carefully measures powders into small bowls, a bundle of labeled palm leaves open beside him.

dialogue.text: For each ailment, recipes: warming pastes for stiff limbs, cooling drenches for fever, fumigations for insects; doses weighed not by scales of brass but by long habit and recorded rule.

i18n.hi: हर रोग के लिए नुस्खे – ठिठुरे अंगों को गरमाने लेप, ज्वार में ठंडे घोट, कीड़ों के लिए धूपन – खुराक तौली जाती है पीतल के बाट से नहीं, लम्बी साधना और लिखे नियम से।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of a warhorse sweating and restless before a campaign, surrounded by armed riders as Shalihotra Vaidya steps in
panels.action: A powerful warhorse tosses its head, flanks dark with sweat, as armored riders glance anxiously toward the gate; Shalihotra Vaidya steps in between, hand raised, calm amid the tension.

dialogue.text: On the eve of a march, one stallion shivers and refuses feed; a single horse, yet his weakness threatens an entire squadron’s speed and the plan drawn on a king’s map.

i18n.hi: कूच की रात, एक अश्व काँपता है, चारा छोड़ देता है – बस एक घोड़ा, पर उसकी कमजोरी से पूरी टुकड़ी की रफ्तार और राजा के नक्शे पर बनी योजना डोल जाती है।

panels.shot: tight medium of Shalihotra Vaidya examining the restless horse’s chest and breath while an impatient commander watches
panels.action: Shalihotra Vaidya presses his ear to the horse’s chest and counts its breaths, then runs his hand along the belly, while a mail-clad commander stands nearby, arms folded, jaw tight.

dialogue.speaker: shalihotra_tradition
dialogue.text: If he rides tonight, you will lose him by dawn—and perhaps the battle.

i18n.hi: आज इसे दौड़ाओगे, तो भोर तक घोड़ा भी जाएगा – और शायद जंग भी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shalihotra Vaidya applying a poultice and instructing grooms, while the commander reluctantly nods
panels.action: Shalihotra Vaidya binds a herbal poultice around the horse’s chest as grooms steady the animal; the commander, still tense, gives a curt nod and signals for another mount.

dialogue.text: The texts speak of when to rest a horse and when to work it, of choosing substitutes and rotating mounts, binding strategy and stable in a single, sober decision.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ बताते हैं कब घोड़े को विश्राम देना है, कब काम, कब बदलूँ लगाम और सवार, ताकि रण-नीति और अस्तबल एक ठंडी, सोच-समझकर ली गई झपट बने।

panels.shot: wide shot of cavalry thundering across open country, with a smaller inset-like visual of the same horses resting and being tended
panels.action: A long line of cavalry races across open grassland, dust rising around them, while in a subtle overlay the same horses are later shown unsaddled, being watered and rubbed down in camp.

dialogue.text: Behind every charge that chroniclers praise, there were intervals of rest, feeding and grooming; disciplines of care that Shalihotra’s tradition quietly codified.

i18n.hi: हर उस धावे के पीछे, जिसे इतिहासकार गाते हैं, बीच-बीच में आराम, खिलाना और सँवारना था – देखभाल की वही अनुशासन, जिन्हें शालिहोत्र परंपरा ने चुपचाप नियम बनाया।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a later-era manuscript workshop, with a scribe copying Shalihotra text as Shalihotra Vaidya appears as a framed painting on the wall
panels.action: In a medieval scriptorium, a scribe bends over a palm-leaf manuscript, copying slanting letters labeled as Shalihotra’s work, while above him hangs a painted panel of Shalihotra Vaidya beside a horse.

dialogue.text: Over centuries, scribes in courts and caravansarais copied and reworked these manuals, folding new cures, new breeds, new routes into the old frame, yet keeping the horse at the center.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक दरबारों और सरायों में लिखारी इन पुस्तकों को नकल और सुधारते रहे – नए इलाज, नस्लें, रास्ते जोड़ते हुए – पर घोड़ा हमेशा बीच में रखा।

panels.shot: wide shot of a port city with horses being led off a ship and into quarantine-like stables, scholars and traders nearby
panels.action: In a busy harbor, handlers lead unfamiliar, high-spirited horses down planks from a foreign ship into waiting stables, while traders bargain and a scholar notes details on a palm leaf.

dialogue.text: Trade brought new strains and new ailments; Shalihotra’s successors watched, compared and added, aware that a disease stepping off a ship could race along the king’s highways in weeks.

i18n.hi: व्यापार नए नस्ल और नई बीमारियाँ लाया; शालिहोत्र के उत्तराधिकारी देखते, तौलते, जोड़ते रहे – जानते थे, जहाज़ से उतरी व्याधि हफ्तों में राजा की सड़कों पर दौड़ सकती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Shalihotra Vaidya’s weathered face morphing subtly into the faces of modern veterinary students examining an X-ray of a horse
panels.action: Shalihotra Vaidya’s lined, intent face fills the frame, then blends into the faces of modern students in a clinical room, studying a horse’s limb X-ray held against bright light.

dialogue.text: Their knowledge is not ours, and their remedies are not a modern clinic’s, yet the same questions echo: how to see suffering early, how to prevent, and how to keep the animal’s strength.

i18n.hi: उनका ज्ञान हमारा नहीं, उनकी दवा आज की क्लिनिक नहीं, पर वही सवाल गूँजते हैं – दर्द जल्दी कैसे पहचाने, बीमारी कैसे रोके, और जानवर की ताकत कैसे बचाए।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Shalihotra Vaidya walking a recovered horse out of the stable at dawn, silhouettes of city, fields and road in the distance
panels.action: At dawn, Shalihotra Vaidya leads a calm, healthy horse out of the stable into soft light, the silhouettes of city walls, fields and a long road stretching away behind him.

dialogue.text: The Shalihotra tradition reminds us that the measure of a civilization is not only in the cities it builds or the wars it wages, but in the quiet care it gives to the animals that bear its journeys.

i18n.hi: शालिहोत्र परंपरा याद दिलाती है – सभ्यता की कसौटी सिर्फ उसके नगर या उसके युद्ध नहीं, वह चुप देखभाल भी है जो वह अपने सफ़रों का भार उठाते जानवरों को देती है।

title_i18n.hi: शालिहोत्र और युद्ध के घोड़े की सेवा

subtitle_i18n.en: How the Horse-Doctor’s Science Rode Beside Kings
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे घोड़ा-वैद्य का ज्ञान राजाओं के संग दौड़ा
